title: Synthetic-Augmented Contrastive Anchor Sampler for Per-Domain Calibration Bundles
creator: Priya Narayanan
description: Design and implement a sampling pipeline that produces compact, per-domain calibration bundles optimized for FP8/INT8 quantization workflows. The sampler should prioritize semantic diversity, edge-case (failure-mode) coverage, and representativeness of high-traffic intents while using lightweight synthetic augmentation to fill sparse regions. Output: deterministic per-domain .tar bundles consumable by the calibration pipeline with metadata for sample provenance and augmentation provenance.
motivation: Current calibration packs either over-represent high-frequency templates or rely on naive stratified sampling that misses rare but high-error examples after quantization. This increases the risk of silent accuracy regressions when rolling low-bit profiles. We need a sampler that deliberately surfaces potential quantization failure modes and produces compact, reproducible packs that match production domain distributions.
goals: (1) Produce per-domain calibration packs of configurable size (default 3k examples) that maximize coverage of semantic clusters and high-error examples. (2) Integrate synthetic augmentation to boost rare intents while preserving label fidelity. (3) Provide sample-level metadata (embedding centroid, sampling weight, augmentation tag, error-priority score) for downstream validators.
out_of_scope: Full retraining of models, generating large synthetic corpora (>10k per domain), on-device client-side sampling, and change to runtime quantization kernels. This ticket focuses on the curation/sampling pipeline and metadata contracts.
success_metrics: (1) Calibration pack size meets target within ±10%. (2) When used to generate calibration tables for FP8/INT8, median per-domain perplexity delta vs float32 < 1.5x and 95th-percentile per-domain delta < 2.5x across validation workloads. (3) Detectable coverage of known historical failure modes: recall of recorded high-error cases in the pack >= 85% when those examples exist in the source window. (4) End-to-end pack generation time < 30 minutes for domains with 10M requests/day when run on a standard staging cluster.
design_decisions: (1) Use a two-stage cluster+contrastive seed selection: coarse k-means on embeddings to form semantic tiles, then contrastive nearest-neighbor scoring to identify boundary cases. (2) Error-priority anchors: seed selection includes examples with high quantization-induced label shifts from previous runs (error gradient). (3) Synthetic augmentation: constrained paraphrase generation with temperature=0.8 and n=2 per seed for rare clusters only, followed by a semantic similarity filter (min cosine 0.82). (4) Per-domain reservoirs: keep a small tail-reservoir for long-tail intents to avoid losing rare but important cases.
sampling_algorithm: 1) Ingest 30-day production prompt logs with minimal PII hashing and per-tenant domain tags. 2) Compute dense embeddings (production embed model v2) and coarse cluster via k-means per-domain (k tuned to domain volume). 3) Rank cluster members by traffic-weighted novelty and historical quantization error score. 4) Select N_seed per cluster (proportional to cluster mass but floor 3). 5) Perform contrastive selection inside each cluster to pick boundary/ambiguous prompts (maximizes pairwise embedding distance). 6) For clusters below rarity threshold, generate synthetic paraphrases (constrained LM) and filter by similarity and token-length distribution. 7) Merge seed+augmented examples, apply reservoir sampling for tail intents, and finalize to target pack size using importance reweighting (traffic * error_priority).
evaluation_plan: (1) Offline simulation: run the sampler on historical 90-day windows and measure recall of known regression signals and embedding coverage. (2) Calibration validation: apply resulting packs to calibration pipeline (FP8/INT8) and measure metric deltas vs float baseline: token-level KL, perplexity, exact-match for structured outputs. (3) A/B test on staging inference fleet: deploy quantized model using new calibration tables and compare latency/cost and quality against current baseline on a fixed eval set. (4) Human spot-checks: 200 random samples per domain reviewed for label swap or hallucination introduced by augmentation.
acceptance_criteria: (1) Pack generation pipeline runs end-to-end on staging and produces per-domain tarballs with metadata JSON and provenance logs. (2) At least one domain demonstrates reduced 95th-percentile perplexity delta post-calibration compared to current packs. (3) Augmentation-induced label errors < 0.5% on human spot-checks. (4) Documentation updated: sampling params, provenance schema, and runbook for reproducing packs.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Internal validation on 3 non-critical domains (week 1). Phase 2: Extended run across 10 domains including an enterprise tenant in staging, collect metrics and smoke test (week 2). Phase 3: Promote to canary in Dedicated cluster with guardrail rollbacks (week 3). Full rollout gated on meeting success metrics and security review sign-off.
implementation_todo: - Build embedding ingestion job with vector store snapshotting. - Implement k-means tiling with dynamic k heuristics. - Implement contrastive boundary scorer. - Integrate constrained LM paraphraser with similarity filter. - Add provenance metadata schema and pack serializer. - Add integration test that runs sampler on a synthetic domain and validates pack size and metadata correctness.
notes: - We must ensure no raw PII leaves the environment: hash/signature and store only hashed identifiers in packs. - Use deterministic random seeds for reproducibility. - Consider adding a lightweight adversarial generator later to stress boundary behavior. - Coordinate with console team for displaying pack provenance and size breakdown.
